content.text: All angles are in for #1325. The verdict is request-changes — real correctness defects on top of solid structure. Consolidating and posting:

input.command:
cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/8ebf5f39-aa39-4923-bd80-44a6e90ca51a/scratchpad/review1325.md << 'EOF'
## /code-review — 7-angle fan-out, consolidated (high effort)

**Verdict: request changes.** The architecture (SampleSpec on the run-target, per-result `sampling` record, refuse-don't-ignore at save time, freshness exemption) is right, and the measurements are honest. But the fan-out found six correctness defects — three on the feature's own headline path — plus two coverage gaps that reintroduce the exact failure classes this PR exists to close.

### Must-fix (correctness)

**C1 — TABLESAMPLE percent formats in scientific notation on large tables.** `unity_catalog.py:360`: the percent is interpolated via Python float repr, which flips to scientific below 1e-4 — and Databricks accepts only INTEGER/DECIMAL literals. `random rows=100` on a 200M-row table emits `TABLESAMPLE (6e-05 PERCENT)` → PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR; even the `_MIN_SAMPLE_PERCENT` floor renders as `1e-06`. The very-large-table case — the reason this feature exists — fails deterministically. Fix: fixed-point formatting (e.g. `f"{percent:.6f}"` with a floor that survives it).

**C2 — UC `seed` is accepted, stamped on the result, and never used.** `unity_catalog.py:358`: the docs promise "add seed to make a run reproducible", `parse_sample_spec` accepts seed for random, and `sampling_record` persists it — but the emitted SQL has no `REPEATABLE(seed)`, so consecutive runs draw different rows while the result claims reproducibility. Emit `REPEATABLE(seed)` or refuse seed on UC; do not stamp what wasn't honored.

**C3 — empty Bernoulli draw → vacuous all-green.** `unity_catalog.py:373`: for small `rows`, P(zero rows) is material (~30% at expected 1.2 rows); an empty frame passes every column expectation vacuously with `rows=0, sampled=true` and a green run — the "all-green on no rows" outcome the `_MIN_SAMPLE_PERCENT` comment promises can't happen. Guard the result: empty (or grossly short) sampled frame → `error`/`skip` with a DataQ-authored message, or re-draw with a raised percent.

**C4 — CSV head window cut is not quote-aware.** `flatfile.py:599`: the window is cut at the last raw `\n`; on CSVs with quoted fields containing newlines the cut can land inside quotes → pandas `ParserError` ("EOF inside string") or silent tail mis-parse — on files the full read handles fine, intermittently by layout. `csv_row_count` uses pyarrow precisely because a newline is not a row boundary; the head path needs the same property (pyarrow-based head, or quote-aware trim).

**C5 — dry-run swallows `ScanTooLargeError` into the generic message.** `dryrun_service.py:218`: the blanket `except` classifies it → "dry run could not execute", with no cap size and no "set a sampling strategy" remedy — while this PR's own comment says the preview must refuse for the same reason. Fix alongside **C6**: `run_service._failure_reason` special-cases `ScanTooLargeError` by isinstance, but the codebase already has the marker for exactly this — `SafeMonitorError` (which `ScanTooLargeError` subclasses), already trusted verbatim at `monitors.py:761` and `anomaly.py:385`. One shared `safe_failure_reason(exc)` helper branching on `SafeMonitorError` serves run + dry-run with one policy instead of a third, narrower copy.

**C6 — table-row-count expectations silently measure the sample.** `flatfile.py:1065`: `expect_table_row_count_to_be_between` against a sampled frame deterministically observes the sample size — a healthy 5M-row file with `min_value=4M` fails critically forever (and the inverse passes wrongly). Monitors were exempted for exactly this smaller-aggregate reason; row-count expectations weren't. Mirror the freshness treatment: refuse the combination at save time (and at run time for pre-existing suites), with a clear message.

**C7 — the comparison path accepts a `sampling` block and silently drops it.** `comparison_run.py:69` / `check_service.py:479`: a comparison check's `source` goes through `resolve_target`, which now validates and ACCEPTS `sampling` — then `DatasetSpec` drops it. Save succeeds, the author believes the read is bounded, the run materializes everything. This is precisely the "silently-dropped sampling block" failure the registry docstring says the 422 exists to prevent. Fix: refuse `sampling` in comparison source specs at save time (threading it through DatasetReader is follow-up scale).

**C8 — MCP read surface can't say "passed on a sample".** `mcp/server.py:234`: `get_suite_results` builds its payload by hand and wasn't extended with `sampling` — an AI client confidently reports full-dataset quality from a 2% sample, the #424/#1115 overclaim class reintroduced for every MCP consumer. Add the field.

### Fix-or-file (judgment call, but every one dispositioned)

**J1 — mutable-object two-pass random (flatfile):** `row_count()` then a second stream; a re-uploaded landing-zone file between passes yields a silently short/skewed sample with a stale `total_rows`. Cheap honesty fix: compare rows-walked vs counted total and refuse/annotate on mismatch (ETag pin is the deluxe version).
**J2 — `dataset_reader.py:219` flat-file comparison read is uncapped** — downloads the whole object before its row-cap check, so the #755 OOM survives via any comparison on an oversized object, and the PR's config comment ("never the current behaviour") overclaims. The preflight it says doesn't exist now does (`file_stat`). Apply the byte-cap preflight there, or correct the claim and file.
**J3 — Iceberg runner is a third full-load runner with no probe, no cap, no sampling** — `RUN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS` claims to govern materialization but skips one of three materializing runners; #755 stays open there. Sampling exclusion was deliberate and fine; the cap wasn't. Cheap version: `scan().count()` probe + row cap refusal. In-PR or file with explicit AC.
**J4 — sample ≥ total degenerate case:** `sampling.py:144` returns `list(range(total))` (~40MB for 1.4M rows) and `take_indices` gather-copies every batch — for a "sample" that changes nothing. Skip selection when `rows >= total`.
**J5 — capability set vs `**_` swallow:** `SAMPLING_CAPABLE_TYPES` (registry) is uncoupled from whether a builder actually threads `sampling`; `_snowflake_runner`/`_iceberg_runner` swallow it via `**_`. A test asserting set-membership ⇔ kwarg-threading (or a runner-level `supports_sampling`) closes the add-to-set-forget-the-builder trap.

### File as follow-ups (structural, not this PR)
- Efficiency batch: CSV random single-pass (reservoir/Algorithm L), head-loop delta fetch instead of re-fetch-from-0, sniff through the reader, per-chunk store-client construction in `read_range` (pre-existing, now hot), HEAD-memo threading into the sampled readers.
- Reuse batch: `object_size` vs `file_stat`; `read_csv_head` vs `_csv_head_frame`; stream-construction dedup (count vs take must share one parse — this one borders correctness: a ParseOptions drift between the two makes random selection off-by-N); UC cap probe vs `dataset_reader`'s ADR-0015 machinery + `row_count_from_scalar`; `_whole_number` vs `_anomaly_int`; `qualified_sql_name` vs `core_table` guts; head-epilogue triplication; `_load_frame` policy duplication; settings read inside the datasources layer.
- Simplification batch: dead `reached_eof` branch, `file_last_modified` wrapper with zero prod callers, `_guard_object_size` stat param vs memo, 3× `enforce_*_cap` copies, `parse_sample_spec` dead None branch.

### Deferred by design (accepted)
- UI authoring + sampled badge: explicitly the #318/UI batch's scope; the API returns what the badge needs. Tracked, not lost.

### Verified-benign (recorded)
Conventions angle: clean — migration is the accepted nullable-add-with-same-PR-read pattern; `sampling` JSONB is read metadata, not a `metric_value` violation; commits well-formed. The head `rows+1` boundary math, `stamp_sampling` reconstruction losslessness, cap `0`-disables paths, and `sampled` edge cases (rows==total, empty file) all checked out correct. CSV random count-vs-take parse consistency verified at head (but see the reuse note about keeping it that way).

J1–J5: fix the cheap ones in-PR (J1 mismatch detection, J4 skip-take when rows>=total, J5 capability⇔threading test; J2 byte-cap preflight in dataset_reader if genuinely small), and FILE a proper issue for anything you don't fix — every J item ends fixed or filed, named in your disposition reply.

The advertised safety net has never been exercised through a genuinely failed statement: the API fake raises RuntimeError from Python (test_suites.py refuse_batched), and the pg end-to-end test monkeypatches build_batched_top_values_query to throw BEFORE any SQL runs — precisely the repo's 'a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing' shape.     "file": "backend/app/services/profile_service.py",
    "line": 665,

The right depth is catching SQLAlchemyError/DBAPIError around the execute only, letting our own code's exceptions raise.",
    "failure_scenario": "A defect in collect_batched_top_values ships, all tests that route through the fallback still return correct results, prod runs N+1 indefinitely (#327 un-fixed in practice), and the only signal is a warning event nobody alerts on.   },

The standing practice recorded in the same file — \"'merged' is not 'deployed', and 'deployed' is not 'works' — verify a fix against the running artifact AND against observed behavior before reporting it as done\" — says this should stay open (or a live-verification follow-up filed) until the SF/UC runs happen.",

## /code-review — 4-angle fan-out, consolidated (medium effort)

**Verdict: request changes.** The rank-driver design and the pg equivalence suite are genuinely strong (the UNION-ALL trap discovery earned its keep). But three angles independently found the same fatal flaw in the safety net, one angle found a silent-wrong-results alias capture, and the fallback's failure economics regress the pre-PR ceiling.

### Must-fix

**P1 — the fallback executes on the aborted transaction; it is dead code on transactional dialects.** `profile_service.py:680`: after a server-side rejection of the batched statement, `_top_values_per_column` reuses the SAME connection with no `rollback()`. Under SQLAlchemy autobegin, Postgres-family engines abort the open transaction — every fallback query then raises `InFailedSqlTransaction` and the profile 502s where pre-#327 code profiled fine. **Empirically reproduced against the live local Postgres.** Neither covering test can see it: the API fake raises from Python pre-execute, and the pg test monkeypatches the builder to raise BEFORE any SQL — the repo's "a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing" shape, verbatim. Fix: best-effort `conn.rollback()` (or a fresh connection) before the fallback, plus a pg test that executes a genuinely failing statement first.

**P2 — a column literally named `freq` silently returns fewer top values.** `profile_service.py:340`: the derived table renders `count(*) AS freq … ORDER BY count(*) DESC, freq LIMIT n`. PG/Snowflake resolve the bare `freq` in ORDER BY to the OUTPUT alias (= the count, i.e. no tie-break), while `row_number() OVER (… , freq)` resolves it to the INPUT column — so the LIMIT keeps a tie-set that disagrees with the rank, kept rows can carry `rn > top_n` (join nothing, vanish), and the profile shows fewer values than exist, no error, no fallback. Verified by compile. Fix: label the count `dq_freq` (or order by the ordinal/expression) and add a `freq` column to the pg equivalence test's `_COLUMNS`.

**P3 — the try-block swallows our own reader's bugs into permanent silent degradation.** `profile_service.py:665`: the catch wraps `collect_batched_top_values` (pure Python) too, so a shipped reader defect silently routes every profile through the N+1 path forever, with one warning nobody alerts on — #327 un-fixed in practice while all tests stay green. Catch `SQLAlchemyError`/`DBAPIError` around the execute only.

**P4 — MCP `profile_column` has unbounded `top_n` that now controls statement size.** `mcp/server.py:533`: no `ge/le` (the REST endpoint has `ge=1 le=100`), and the rank driver materializes `top_n` UNION-ALL branches per chunk — `top_n=100000` compiles a multi-MB CompoundSelect in the request thread. LLM-generated args are exactly the callers that do this. Bound it to match REST.

**P5 — all-or-nothing fallback regresses the pre-PR ceiling.** `profile_service.py:664`: chunk 2 of 2 failing discards chunk 1's results and re-runs ALL columns per-column — 53 round-trips where pre-#327 cost 51, with 25 columns computed twice against the warehouse that just proved slow. Fall back per-chunk (`collected.update(...)` for the failed chunk's columns only), which also dedupes the two `_top_values_per_column` call sites.

### Should-fix (minor)
- **m1** `top_n < 1` branch: routes to per-column LIMIT-0 queries (N round-trips returning nothing, for an input both API surfaces make unreachable) — `return {}` / `{col: []}` with zero queries.
- **m2** Test fake substring routing: `if col in sql` cross-wires `c1` ↔ `c10`/`c11` if the fallback loop is ever reached — anchor the match (word boundary / `WHERE <col> IS NOT NULL` regex).
- **m3** The pg test's `_per_column` reference helper re-implements the real fallback — call `profile_service._top_values_per_column` so equivalence is proven against the production path.
- **m4** Compose the batched builder FROM `build_top_values_query` (+ `.add_columns(row_number…)`) so "exactly the per-column query plus a rank" is true by construction, retiring the fragment-matching drift test.
- **m5** Consider `sqlalchemy.values()` for the rank driver instead of a top_n-branch UNION ALL (compact `(VALUES …)` rendering, no type-unification concern) — fold into the live verification below, not a separate pass.

### Carried to live verification (orchestrator, pre-merge)
Per the #953 rule: batched SQL proven on Postgres only. The live Snowflake + UC pass must check (a) correctness of the rank-join, (b) **timing vs the per-column path** — `_TOP_VALUES_BATCH=25` is calibrated on the Postgres planner (the GEQO-at-12-relations cliff is PG machinery); if the warehouses' cliff sits lower, the batch could be slower than the N+1 it replaces with zero signal, since success doesn't trigger the fallback.

### Verified-benign (recorded)
Single-element `union_all` compiles for top_n=1; `folding_identifier` quotes without lowercasing so the fake's lookups match; omitted empty-column keys safe (`assemble_profile.get(col, [])` is the sole consumer); dialect/catalog threading identical to the removed inline path; lowercase `rn`/`v_0`/`f_0` labels follow the proven `nulls_0` normalization precedent; columns named `rn`/`value` benign; fallback warning logs exception type only (no SQL/values — PII-clean).

# Local DataQ ⟷ prod mirror — session summary + runbook

**Session: 2026-08-03.** DataQ's local dev stack was converted into a live
mirror of prod (real secrets, real connections/suites, real datasource
traffic) and the local harness stack (this repo's `local/`) was brought up
alongside it. This doc is the replication runbook for redoing that, plus
guidance on using the mirror day-to-day and on actually exercising the local
Airflow/MinIO stack (which, as of this session, sits up but **unused** — see
§4).

Companion: DataQ's own memory note
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-arijit-Coding-Python-DataQ/memory/project_local_prod_mirror_setup.md`
carries the same gotchas for AI-assistant sessions; this file is the
human-readable, repo-anchored version.

---

## 1. What was done this session

1. **Brought up DataQ's own compose stack** (`docker compose up -d` in
   `~/Coding/Python/DataQ`) — postgres/redis/openbao/mailpit/api/worker/frontend,
   all default services.
2. **Brought up this repo's local harness** (`local/harness_local.sh up`) —
   Airflow (Postgres+Redis+CeleryExecutor) + MinIO, joined onto DataQ's
   compose network.
3. **Configured multi-user email-OTP sign-in** by setting `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL`
   in DataQ's root `.env` — see the gotcha in §2.2, this is the ONE switch,
   not a separately-settable allowlist.
4. **Mirrored local OpenBao onto Azure Key Vault exactly** — purged 143
   unrelated stale secrets from a prior local session, wrote in the 25 real
   `dataq-app-kv-aw6laj` secrets by name (values piped directly between `az`
   and OpenBao's HTTP API, never printed or written to disk), verified the
   name sets are now identical.
5. **Replaced local DB seed/demo data with prod's real `users` /
   `connections` / `suites` / `checks`** — nuked the local schema, re-ran
   migrations, opened a **temporary** Postgres firewall rule, copied the four
   tables straight from prod via `psycopg2`, closed the firewall rule
   immediately after. 13 connections, 12 suites, 30 checks, 8 users.
6. **Verified functionality**: OTP sign-in end-to-end (Mailpit), suite runs
   across Snowflake / ADLS flat-file / Unity Catalog (all green, including a
   deliberately-seeded prod failure behaving as expected) / Iceberg (failed —
   see §2.5, expected given the closed firewall rule).
7. **Backfilled asset resolution** — the raw DB copy bypassed the service
   layer that normally creates an `assets` row on suite save, so `GET
   /assets` was empty. Fixed by re-`PATCH`ing each suite with its own
   existing `target`, which forces `resolve_and_upsert_asset` without
   changing anything else. 10 assets now exist, correctly deduplicated.
8. **Reset a latent lineage-sync landmine** — the copied Unity Catalog
   connections carried prod's *incremental* lineage watermark
   (`2026-07-27`) into a local DB whose `lineage_edges` table was never
   copied. Left alone, a future local warehouse-lineage refresh would have
   silently started from that stale cursor and permanently skipped
   everything before it. Reset `lineage_watermark` /
   `lineage_last_refresh_at` / `lineage_last_tier` to `NULL` on both UC
   connections.

**Not done (deliberately out of scope):** `trigger_bindings` / `schedules` /
`suite_notifications` / access-grants were not copied from prod — local
suites won't auto-fire on a cron or an orchestration trigger. Lineage edges
themselves were not copied and are not backfilled (they only populate via a
live refresh, which is off locally by default — same as prod).

---

## 2. Replication runbook (redo this from scratch)

Run this in `~/Coding/Python/DataQ` unless noted. Requires `az` logged in
with Key Vault read + Container App secret read + the shared Postgres
server's firewall-rule permissions (deployer/`dataq-admin`-tier access).

### 2.1 Bring up both stacks

```bash
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ
docker compose up -d                       # postgres/redis/openbao/mailpit/api/worker/frontend

cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/local
./harness_local.sh up                      # requires DataQ's stack up first (joins dataq_default)
```

### 2.2 Multi-user OTP sign-in

`.env`'s `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` **is** the allowlist — `docker-compose.yml`
wires it straight into `AUTH_OTP_ALLOWED_EMAILS` verbatim
(`${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL?...}`, not a separate override). Comma-separate it for
multiple users:

```bash
# .env is deliberately unwritable by the Edit tool in an AI session (secrets
# guard) — append with a shell redirect instead:
printf 'DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL=you@example.com,teammate@example.com\n' >> .env
docker compose up -d api worker             # env is a start-time snapshot
```

`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` defaults to `dev-bypass@dataq.local,${DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL}`
— so every signed-in address is workspace-admin by default, which is what
gives a freshly-provisioned local user visibility into prod's suites (they
belong to prod's *user rows*, not to whichever new email you sign in with;
workspace-admin has implicit visibility into everything, ADR 0027).

### 2.3 Mirror OpenBao onto Key Vault (exact set, no extras)

```bash
KV=dataq-app-kv-aw6laj   # re-verify with `az keyvault list` in case it's been renamed
source .env.app          # OPENBAO_ADDR / OPENBAO_MOUNT / OPENBAO_TOKEN

az keyvault secret list --vault-name "$KV" --query "[?attributes.enabled].name" -o tsv | sort > /tmp/kv_names.txt

curl -s -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/metadata?list=true" \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; print('\n'.join(sorted(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['keys'])))" > /tmp/local_names.txt

# purge anything local-only
comm -23 /tmp/local_names.txt /tmp/kv_names.txt | while read -r n; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -X DELETE -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/metadata/$n"
done

# write in every KV secret (value piped straight through, never echoed/printed)
while read -r n; do
  az keyvault secret show --vault-name "$KV" --name "$n" --query value -o tsv \
    | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.dumps({'data':{'value': sys.stdin.readline().rstrip(chr(10))}}))" \
    | curl -s -o /dev/null -X POST -H "X-Vault-Token: $OPENBAO_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      --data-binary @- "$OPENBAO_ADDR/v1/$OPENBAO_MOUNT/data/$n"
done < /tmp/kv_names.txt
```

**Gotcha:** this purge also deletes `dataq-local-smtp` — the bundled Mailpit
catcher's password, seeded locally by the one-shot `otp-mail-secret` compose
service. It never exists in prod Key Vault by design (prod mails via Gmail
SMTP under different secret names), so a strict "match KV exactly" diff
always removes it, and OTP sign-in then fails with
`otp_email_not_configured`. Fix, every time:

```bash
docker compose up -d --force-recreate otp-mail-secret
```

### 2.4 Wipe local seed data, pull in prod's real data

```bash
cd ~/Coding/Python/DataQ

# 1. temp access to the shared prod Postgres server
MYIP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org)
az postgres flexible-server firewall-rule create -g dataq-rg --server-name dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd \
  --name "temp-local-sync-$(python3 -c 'import time;print(int(time.time()))')" \
  --start-ip-address "$MYIP" --end-ip-address "$MYIP"

# 2. resolve prod's DATABASE_URL — it is NOT in any tfvars file (apply-time-only var);
#    read it straight off the live Container App secret instead:
export PROD_DATABASE_URL=$(az containerapp secret list -n dataq-app-api -g dataq-rg --show-values -o json \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next(s['value'] for s in d if s['name']=='database-url'))")

# 3. nuke local schema, re-migrate (NO reseed — that's exactly the demo data being removed)
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U dataq -d dataq -c "DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;"
export LOCAL_DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"
(cd backend && DATABASE_URL="$LOCAL_DATABASE_URL" conda run -n dataq alembic upgrade head)
# Gotcha: `conda run -n dataq sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"` alone fails with
# "no password supplied" — pydantic-settings' env_file=".env.app" resolves relative to cwd,
# and there is no backend/.env.app (only the repo-root one). Export DATABASE_URL explicitly.

"""Live verification of PR #1323's batched top-values SQL vs Snowflake + UC.

Runs the PR-branch code (agent worktree) against the REAL warehouses via the
local mirror DB's connection rows + OpenBao secrets. Per the #953 rule.

Checks per warehouse:
  1. Batched path == per-column path (values AND types), via the production
     functions themselves.
  2. Timing: batched vs per-column wall clock (the GEQO-cliff concern).
  3. The full profile_table() production entry point succeeds.

Never prints secret values. Prints only table/column names, counts, timings,
equality verdicts.
"""

import os
import sys
import time

WORKTREE = "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/.claude/worktrees/agent-a22d75afd904f1655"
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(WORKTREE, "backend"))

os.environ["DATABASE_URL"] = "REDACTED"

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text  # noqa: E402
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session  # noqa: E402

from app.core.secrets import get_secret_store  # noqa: E402
from app.db.models import Connection  # noqa: E402
from app.services import profile_service  # noqa: E402
from app.services.profile_service import (  # noqa: E402
    _fetch_top_values,
    _open_connection,
    _top_values_per_column,
    profile_table,
)

TARGETS = {
    "snowflake": {"table": "ORDERS_HEADER", "schema": "RETAIL", "catalog": None},
    "unity_catalog": {
        "table": "feedback_sentiment",
        "schema": "gold",
        "catalog": "dataq_retail",
    },
}

TOP_N = 10


def columns_for(conn, dialect_name, schema, table, catalog):
    if dialect_name == "snowflake":
        q = text(
            "SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns "
            "WHERE table_schema = :s AND table_name = :t ORDER BY ordinal_position"
        )
        rows = conn.execute(q, {"s": schema, "t": table}).fetchall()
    else:
        q = text(
            f"SELECT column_name FROM {catalog}.information_schema.columns "
            "WHERE table_schema = :s AND table_name = :t ORDER BY ordinal_position"
        )
        rows = conn.execute(q, {"s": schema, "t": table}).fetchall()
    return [r[0] for r in rows]


def norm(d):
    return {k: [(str(v), int(c)) for v, c in vals] for k, vals in d.items()}


def main() -> int:
    app_engine = create_engine(os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])
    store = get_secret_store()
    failures = 0

    with Session(app_engine) as session:
        conns = (
            session.query(Connection)
            .filter(Connection.type.in_(list(TARGETS)))
            .all()
        )
        by_type = {c.type: c for c in conns}

        for ctype, tgt in TARGETS.items():
            connection = by_type.get(ctype)
            if connection is None:
                print(f"[{ctype}] NO CONNECTION ROW — skip")
                failures += 1
                continue
            print(f"\n=== {ctype}: {connection.name} -> "
                  f"{tgt['catalog'] or ''}.{tgt['schema']}.{tgt['table']} ===")
            try:
                with _open_connection(connection, store) as conn:
                    dialect = conn.dialect
                    cols = columns_for(
                        conn, dialect.name, tgt["schema"], tgt["table"], tgt["catalog"]
                    )
                    print(f"columns ({len(cols)}): {cols}")

                    t0 = time.perf_counter()
                    per_col = _top_values_per_column(
                        conn,
                        schema=tgt["schema"],
                        table=tgt["table"],
                        columns=cols,
                        top_n=TOP_N,
                        catalog=tgt["catalog"],
                        dialect=dialect,
                    )
                    t_per = time.perf_counter() - t0

                    t0 = time.perf_counter()
                    batched = _fetch_top_values(
                        conn,
                        schema=tgt["schema"],
                        table=tgt["table"],
                        columns=cols,
                        top_n=TOP_N,
                        catalog=tgt["catalog"],
                        dialect=dialect,
                    )
                    t_bat = time.perf_counter() - t0

                    equal = norm(per_col) == norm(batched)
                    print(f"equivalence (values+counts, {len(cols)} cols): "
                          f"{'PASS' if equal else 'FAIL'}")
                    if not equal:
                        failures += 1
                        for c in cols:
                            a, b = norm(per_col).get(c), norm(batched).get(c)
                            if a != b:
                                print(f"  DIFF {c}: per-column={a} batched={b}")
                    # type fidelity: compare python types positionally
                    tmatch = all(
                        [type(v).__name__ for v, _ in per_col.get(c, [])]
                        == [type(v).__name__ for v, _ in batched.get(c, [])]
                        for c in cols
                    )
                    print(f"type fidelity: {'PASS' if tmatch else 'FAIL'}")
                    if not tmatch:
                        failures += 1
                    print(
                        f"timing: per-column {t_per:.2f}s ({len(cols)} round-trips) "
                        f"vs batched {t_bat:.2f}s "
                        f"({(len(cols) + 24) // 25 + 0} chunk round-trip(s)) "
                        f"-> {'batched FASTER' if t_bat < t_per else 'batched SLOWER'}"
                    )
                    if t_bat > t_per:
                        print("  WARNING: batched slower than per-column on this "
                              "warehouse — the GEQO-cliff concern")

                # 3. full production entry point
                t0 = time.perf_counter()
                result = profile_table(
                    connection,
                    table=tgt["table"],
                    schema=tgt["schema"],
                    columns=cols[: min(len(cols), 50)],
                    top_n=TOP_N,
                    secret_store=store,
                    catalog=tgt["catalog"],
                )
                t_full = time.perf_counter() - t0
                ncols = len(result.columns)
                n_top = sum(1 for c in result.columns if c.top_values)
                print(f"profile_table: OK — {ncols} column profiles, "
                      f"{n_top} with top_values, {t_full:.2f}s total")
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                failures += 1
                print(f"[{ctype}] FAILED: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")

    print(f"\n{'ALL PASS' if failures == 0 else f'{failures} FAILURE(S)'}")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

def _recover_transaction(conn: Any) -> None:
    """Roll back so the fallback can run on a usable connection (#327 review, P1).

    A server-side rejection of the batched statement leaves SQLAlchemy's autobegun
    transaction **aborted** on Postgres-family engines: every subsequent statement
    on that connection raises ``InFailedSqlTransaction`` until it is rolled back.
    Without this the fallback was dead code exactly when it was needed — the
    profile 502'd where the pre-#327 per-column path would have succeeded. Not
    theoretical: reproduced against a live Postgres, and pinned by a test that
    executes a genuinely failing statement rather than raising from Python.

    Best-effort by design. The profiler only ever reads, so there is nothing to
    lose by rolling back, and a connection object that cannot (a test double, an
    autocommit-only driver) must not turn a recoverable batch failure into a hard
    one — hence the broad catch and the log instead of a raise.
    """
    try:
        conn.rollback()
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning("profile_top_values_rollback_failed", error_type=type(exc).__name__)


def _fetch_top_values(
    conn: Any,
    *,
    schema: str,
    table: str,
    columns: list[str],
    top_n: int,
    catalog: str | None,
    dialect: Dialect | None,
) -> dict[str, list[Mapping[str, Any]]]:
    """Top values for every column, batched, with the per-column path as fallback.

    Runs `build_batched_top_values_query` in chunks of `_TOP_VALUES_BATCH` — the
    #327 win, turning 1 + N round-trips into 1 + ceil(N / `_TOP_VALUES_BATCH`).

        col: [
            {"value": row[_VALUE_LABEL], "freq": row[_FREQ_LABEL]}
            for row in conn.execute(
                build_top_values_query(schema, table, col, top_n, catalog, dialect)
            ).mappings()
        ]
        for col in columns
    }


def _recover_transaction(conn: Any) -> None:
    """Roll back so the fallback can run on a usable connection (#327 review, P1).

    A server-side rejection of the batched statement leaves SQLAlchemy's autobegun
    transaction **aborted** on Postgres-family engines: every subsequent statement
    on that connection raises ``InFailedSqlTransaction`` until it is rolled back.
    Without this the fallback was dead code exactly when it was needed — the
    profile 502'd where the pre-#327 per-column path would have succeeded. Not
    theoretical: reproduced against a live Postgres, and pinned by a test that
    executes a genuinely failing statement rather than raising from Python.

    Best-effort by design. The profiler only ever reads, so there is nothing to
    lose by rolling back, and a connection object that cannot (a test double, an
    autocommit-only driver) must not turn a recoverable batch failure into a hard
    one — hence the broad catch and the log instead of a raise.
    """
    try:
        conn.rollback()
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning("profile_top_values_rollback_failed", error_type=type(exc).__name__)


def _fetch_top_values(
    conn: Any,
    *,
    schema: str,
    table: str,
    columns: list[str],
    top_n: int,
    catalog: str | None,

    #327 win, turning 1 + N round-trips into 1 + ceil(N / `_TOP_VALUES_BATCH`).

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — DataQ project guide for AI assistants

> Single source of truth for any Claude / AI assistant working in this repo. Read this end-to-end before touching code.

---

## 1. Project summary

**DataQ** is a single-tenant data quality monitoring platform built around Great Expectations (GX Core). It runs DQ checks across **5 datasources** and integrates with **3 orchestration providers**.

| Layer | Components |
|---|---|
| **Datasources (you can write checks against)** | Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT), ADLS Gen2, AWS S3 **and any S3-compatible store** (MinIO/Ceph/R2/Wasabi/Backblaze, via the optional `endpoint_url` — #1063), Unity Catalog (Databricks), Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030) |
| **Orchestration providers (monitor + trigger only — NOT datasources)** | Azure Data Factory (ADF), Apache Airflow, dbt (ADR 0029) |
| **Backend** | FastAPI + Celery + Redis + PostgreSQL + Alembic |
| **Frontend** | React + Vite + Ant Design + Monaco editor (generic OIDC — `oidc-client-ts`) |
| **Auth / secrets** | Three-mode ladder (ADR 0032): dev-bypass (eval) · **email OTP** (IdP-less, default for the local stack — #1150) · OIDC (Azure AD validated; provider-neutral `AUTH_*` contract) — plus PATs (`dq_live_`) for API/MCP clients. Secrets: Azure Key Vault / OpenBao (ADR 0039) |
| **Deploy** | Azure Container Apps (API + worker + frontend; frontend is the sole public surface, api internal — ADR 0028 §5) |
| **Observability** | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
| **AI integration** | FastMCP (8 curated tools mounted at `/mcp`) — Claude Desktop / Claude.ai / Copilot / Cursor |

Timeline: **8 weeks** to v1. Scope: single tenant, suite-level access sharing, Azure-hosted.

---

## 2. Architecture at a glance

See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) for the full diagram (Mermaid — renders on GitHub).

```
Browser ──HTTPS──► Frontend Container App (nginx SPA, sole public ingress)
AI clients ──MCP/HTTP──► │  proxies /api + /mcp + /healthz same-origin
                         ▼
                    FastAPI (Container Apps, INTERNAL ingress) ──► PostgreSQL
                         │  │
                         │  └──► Celery worker ──► GX execution ──► Snowflake / ADLS / S3 / UC
                         ├──► Redis (task queue)
                         ├──► Key Vault (secrets)
                         └──► App Insights (observability)

ADF ──► Azure Monitor alert rule ──► webhook ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf ──► (proxied) api
Airflow ──► on_success/on_failure_callback ──► POST <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow ──► (proxied) api
FastAPI ──► MS Teams / Slack / email (alerts, ResultPublisher seam)
```

---

## 3. Repo layout

Flat monorepo (decided in Week 1):

```
DataQ/
├── backend/                     # FastAPI + Celery + GX (Python, conda)
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── core/                # logging, errors, config (locked in PR 2)
│   │   ├── db/                  # SQLAlchemy models, session
│   │   ├── api/                 # FastAPI routers (versioned: /api/v1/...)
│   │   ├── services/            # business logic per domain
│   │   ├── orchestration/       # OrchestrationProvider abstraction (ADF, Airflow)
│   │   ├── datasources/         # ConnectionAdapter + CheckRunner per type; gx_runner.py (shared GX translation), flatfile.py (flat-file IO + runner + batch resolution), sql.py (shared SQL-identifier allowlist — #428)
│   │   └── mcp/                 # FastMCP tools (Week 7)
│   ├── alembic/
│   └── tests/                   # + tests/support/ (adversarial harness), tests/integration/ (end-to-end datasource runs)
├── frontend/                    # React + Vite + Ant Design (Node, pnpm)
│   ├── src/
│   └── tests/
├── docs/
│   ├── architecture.md          # Mermaid architecture diagram
│   └── adr/                     # Architecture Decision Records
├── integrations/                # user-deployed snippets (NOT app code; e.g. Airflow DAG callback)
│   └── airflow/                 # dataq_airflow_callback.py + setup README
├── scripts/
│   └── setup.sh                 # one-command dev env bootstrap
├── context/                     # original product/roadmap context (read-only reference)
│   └── DataQ_platform_roadmap.md
├── .github/
│   ├── workflows/
│   ├── pull_request_template.md
│   ├── CODEOWNERS
│   └── ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
├── docker-compose.yml
├── environment.yml              # conda env — pip section points at backend/requirements-dev.txt
├── pyproject.toml               # Black + Ruff + mypy config
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── CLAUDE.md                    # this file
└── README.md
```

**Promotion to `apps/` + `packages/`:** only if a real shared package emerges (e.g., auto-generated OpenAPI client in Week 4–5). Default flat.

---

## 4. Datasources vs orchestration — critical distinction

**Datasources** are stores you write DQ checks against:
- Snowflake (DEV/QA/UAT)
- ADLS Gen2 (flat files)
- AWS S3 — and any S3-compatible store, via the connection's optional `endpoint_url` (#1063)
- Unity Catalog / Databricks
- Apache Iceberg (native `pyiceberg` read — ADR 0030; engine-registered Iceberg tables also work zero-code under the `snowflake`/`unity_catalog` connections)

**Orchestration providers** are NOT datasources. They are workflow engines whose pipelines/DAGs we observe and react to. Their *only* three responsibilities in DataQ:

1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table (separate from `runs` / `results`).
2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific event channels (webhook for both).
3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings` (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `suite_id`, `env`). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs.

All three providers implement a single `OrchestrationProvider` interface — ADF is the reference implementation, Airflow is the second, dbt (ADR 0029) is the third (artifact-poll + HMAC callback, no host REST API). **Never hardcode ADF-only logic; always go through the abstraction.**

| Provider | Event channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADF | Azure Monitor alert → webhook | Shared secret header (Azure Monitor's only mode) | ADF REST API, 10 min |
| Airflow | DAG `on_*_callback` → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns`, 10 min |
| dbt | post-build callback → webhook | HMAC-signed payload (app-level signing key) | poll `run_results.json` artifact (adls/s3/file), 10 min |

Airflow callbacks require the user to add a snippet to their DAGs (we can't mutate them). Polling is the documented fallback.

**Anti-pattern (do not do this):** treating ADF/Airflow as a 5th/6th datasource in the connection editor, check editor, or suite model.

---

## 5. Framework choice — GX-only for v1

- **v1:** Great Expectations (GX Core) is the sole DQ framework across all datasources. Unifies result schema, suite/check model, MCP tools, and the check editor. Every v1 check is a GX **expectation** (`check.kind = 'expectation'`).
- **v1.1+:** platform-native engines are **connection-anchored** (ADR [0036](docs/adr/0036-connection-anchored-check-engines.md)): every datasource connection offers GX; a Snowflake connection additionally offers **DMF**, Unity Catalog offers **DQX** (DLT/streaming — GX is batch-only), a future BigQuery type offers **Dataplex**. Engine selection is **per check** (`check.engine`, default `gx`, validated against the connection's capability set; `kind` stays orthogonal to `engine`) — supersedes the earlier suite-level `engine: gx | dqx` toggle sketch. DMF is the first native build; DQX/Dataplex are trigger-gated (see the ADR §6).
- **Monitor-kind seam (do-now, Week 3):** not every monitor is a GX expectation. A `check.kind` discriminator (`expectation` in v1; `freshness | volume | schema_drift | anomaly | comparison` reserved — freshness/volume shipped post-v1 (#426/#437) and **`comparison` shipped v1.1 W3** (ADR 0015, #791–#795) and **`schema_drift` shipped v1.1 W4** (#592) and **`anomaly` shipped v1.1 W5** (#593, rolling z-score baseline with optional seasonality, PRs #1117/#1119)) + numeric `metric_value` on results let v1.x auto-monitors slot in without a check/result schema rewrite. This seam is **orthogonal to the datasource seams** (`CheckRunner`, `ConnectionAdapter`): it varies by *monitor kind*, not datasource. See ADR `0012` (and `0014` for the reserved `comparison` / cross-dataset reconciliation kind) and post-v1 roadmap Theme A. Most real incidents are freshness/volume, not value-level — this is the leap from "GX runner" to DQ platform.
- **DQ-dimension axis (v1.1 W4, ADR [0038](docs/adr/0038-dq-dimension-classification.md)):** every check also carries a `dimension` — accuracy / completeness / consistency / integrity / timeliness / uniqueness / validity — a **third axis orthogonal to both `kind` (how the monitor works) and `engine` (what evaluates it)**. Closed vocabulary via table `CHECK`; derived by default from the check type, **stored** (so #889 aggregates in SQL and an override survives), and overridable at any time. Derivation is **deliberately partial** — `accuracy`/`integrity` are never derivable from a rule shape and custom SQL is an arbitrary predicate — so **NULL means unclassified and must render as a coverage gap**, never silently bucketed. Existing rows were backfilled (#952, §5 amended). It is the input to the asset DQ scorecard (#889), whose value is *coverage* ("this asset has no Timeliness checks") more than score.
- **Week-3 outcome (done):** the UC run path is thin behind `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` (reads the table into a GX DataFrame asset — the DQX swap-in shape), and `check.kind` + `metric_value`/`duration_ms` shipped in the one threshold migration, so the monitor-kind impls won't ripple into the suite/check/result layer later. **Amended v1.1 W6 (#1179):** the UC runner now builds **two** batches — the DataFrame one for every ordinary expectation, and a GX **Databricks-SQL** batch for custom-SQL checks only. `UnexpectedRowsExpectation`'s metrics have a SqlAlchemy provider and no pandas one, so ADR 0019's UC support had never once worked in a run *or* a dry-run; it is SQL by definition and was never going to be a DQX rule, so the DQX swap-in argument is unaffected for everything it actually covers.

---

## 6. Working agreements (rules above feature work)

Full list (40 rules across 8 categories) lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Highlights:

### Commit & change discipline
Per-functionality workflow, in order:
1. **One functionality per commit** (where possible).
2. **Test coverage for the functionality** (unit/integration as applicable — the ≥80% CI gate, live since Week 8, covers this).
3. **Docs updated if required** (CLAUDE.md / ADR / CONTRIBUTING / user docs — whichever the change touches).
4. **Agentic code-review on the PR** — spawn `/code-review` (never an inline self-review only) and post findings to the PR as inline comments (`/code-review --comment`).
5. **Fix issues found in the same PR** where feasible.
6. **File a GitHub issue for anything deferred** — never drop a finding silently. Use `gh issue create`; the fixing PR must include `Fixes #N`.
7. **Full CI gate must pass** (lint/format/types/tests/security — see below).
8. **Squash-merge to `main`.**

### Git workflow
- **Trunk-based** with short-lived feature branches off `main`. No long-lived `develop`.
- Branch names: `feature/<desc>`, `fix/issue-<N>-<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`, `docs/<desc>`.
- `main` is protected: PR + passing CI + no force-push. (≥1 approving review is disabled during solo-dev phase; re-enable before onboarding a second contributor.)
- **Squash-merge only into `main`.**
- **Conventional commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`).

### CI/CD quality gates (block merge)
- Ruff (lint), Black `--check` (format), mypy (types), pytest (from W8), frontend lint/format/test.
- `betterleaks` secret scanning (pre-commit + CI).
- Bandit (Python SAST) + CodeQL.
- **Dependency CVE audit (CI): `pip-audit -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (full backend runtime + test surface) + `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` (frontend).** Synchronous merge gate; complements the async Dependabot layer below.
- **Python deps have one source of truth: `backend/requirements.txt`** (runtime hub) → `requirements-dev.txt` (`-r` it + test toolchain) → `environment.yml` + CI all install from it. The re-listed subsets `requirements-dev.txt` pulls are `requirements-typecheck.txt` (the typed deps mypy needs) and `requirements-tooling.txt` (Black/Ruff/mypy/Bandit/pre-commit); the `typecheck-deps-sync` check (pre-commit **and** CI `backend-lint`) keeps the mypy hook aligned. `requirements-mutation.txt` (mutmut) is **standalone — not `-r`'d by anything**, so it stays off CI's install + `pip-audit` surface (manual tool, CONTRIBUTING rule 4a). Bump a Python version in `requirements.txt` only.
- Dependabot for npm + pip + github-actions — **version updates + security alerts/updates both enabled** (alerts scan the full pip+npm dependency graph).

### Tooling (locked in Week 1, do not drift)
- **Python:** conda env (`conda create -n dataq python=3.13`) — *not* venv, *not* poetry. (3.13 since ADR 0017; was 3.11.)
- **Black** formatter (CI-enforced).
- **Ruff** lint, **mypy** types, **structlog** logging, **Pydantic Settings** config (12-factor).
- **Frontend:** Prettier + ESLint.

### Observability
- **Structured logging from Week 1.** structlog, JSON, `request_id` correlation propagated FastAPI → Celery → GX.
- **PII redaction at logger level** (failed-check sample rows may contain sensitive data).
- **App Insights exception tracking wired Week 1**, not Week 7.

### Database
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** No `DROP COLUMN` + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward.
- Migration PR checklist: rollback plan + "tested up + down locally."

### Documentation
- **ADRs in `docs/adr/`** — one short markdown per significant decision.
- `scripts/setup.sh` — one command from clone to working dev env.

## 10. Critical pointers (easy to get wrong)

- **`pipeline_runs` ≠ `runs`.** Orchestrator pipeline executions live in `pipeline_runs`; DQ suite executions live in `runs`. They link via `triggered_by: '<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>'`.
- **`trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic.** Composite key (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. Don't add an ADF-specific bindings table.
- **PII redaction at the logger level**, not at every call site. The redactor sits in `backend/app/core/logging.py`.
- **Backward-compatible migrations only.** Code that depends on a new column ships in a separate PR *after* the migration is deployed.
- **The Week-3 threshold migration already added the schema seams (done).** It landed `check.kind` (default `'expectation'`), `results.metric_value` (NUMERIC) + `duration_ms` (INT), and the severity thresholds — see ADR `0012`. `metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; **don't store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`** (you can't `AVG()`/`STDDEV()` it for trends or anomaly baselines), and **don't add a second migration re-introducing these columns**.
- **Secret scanning in pre-commit AND CI.** Don't rely on one alone.
- **Azure Monitor alert setup (Week 7) needs the deployed public API URL.** Deployment must come first; coordinate Container Apps ingress with infra/security before Week 7 to avoid a deployment-day surprise.
- **MCP tool descriptions are LLM-facing, not REST-API-facing.** Write them for natural-language selection; test against the 4 canonical NL queries in the roadmap.

## 11. What NOT to do

- ❌ Don't add ADF or Airflow as a queryable datasource in the connection editor / check editor / suite model.
- ❌ Don't bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction with provider-specific branching in service code.
- ❌ Don't deepen Azure lock-in: no reading Entra/OIDC provider claims in route/service code (depend on the generic `get_current_user`), no hardcoded Azure resource names/endpoints in business logic, no Azure-only assumptions baked into container images. Azure is one impl behind each seam — see ADR [0010](docs/adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) / [0013](docs/adr/0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md).
- ❌ Don't `git commit --no-verify` past hooks. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
- ❌ Don't commit `.env` files. Use `.env.example` / `.env.app.example` as the templates.
- ❌ Don't put a credential — **even a local/mock one** — in any git-tracked file (templates, `scripts/`, CI, compose). Env templates ship the secret keys **blank** with the shape in a comment; `scripts/setup.sh` generates the local-dev password into the gitignored `.env`/`.env.app` on first run. Non-secret config defaults and non-secret identifiers (db/user name) may stay populated.
- ❌ Don't drop columns in the same PR as the code change that stops using them. Two-step it.
- ❌ Don't fix bugs silently. Raise a GitHub issue, then PR with `Fixes #N`.
- ❌ **Don't dismiss a finding because it's pre-existing.** DataQ is in production — a defect that predates your change is live for users right now, so its age is irrelevant to whether it matters. Every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never "noted in a review reply" or "documented in a docstring" (CONTRIBUTING rule 3a). Concluding it is genuinely not a defect is fine, but record the determination and evidence — verified-benign is a valid outcome, unexamined is not.
- ❌ Don't batch unrelated changes into one commit. One functionality per commit.
- ❌ Don't track GX Core at "latest." Pin the version in `environment.yml` — GX v1 API has drifted across point releases.
- ❌ Don't add a dependency under a strong-copyleft or source-available license (GPL, AGPL, SSPL, BUSL/Elastic, Commons-Clause) — DataQ ships MIT (ADR [0031](docs/adr/0031-oss-byol-distribution-licensing.md), CONTRIBUTING rule 40); weak copyleft (LGPL/MPL) is OK with notices. Exceptions need an ADR.
- ❌ Don't use venv or poetry for backend dev. Conda only.
- ❌ Don't write the MCP layer before Week 7. The service layer must stabilise first.

## Appendix — Tech stack quick reference

| Layer | Tech |
|---|---|
| Backend framework | FastAPI (Python 3.13) |
| DQ engine | Great Expectations (GX Core) v1 — **pinned version** |
| Task queue | Celery + Redis |
| Database | PostgreSQL + Alembic |
| Frontend | React + Vite + Ant Design |
| SQL editor | Monaco |
| Auth | Three modes (ADR 0032): dev-bypass · email OTP (`dq_sess_` cookie sessions, local-stack default) · generic OIDC (`oidc-client-ts`, Azure AD validated) + backend `fastapi-azure-auth`; PATs (`dq_live_`) for API/MCP |
| Secrets | Azure Key Vault |
| Hosting | Azure Container Apps (API + worker + frontend; frontend = sole public surface, api internal — ADR 0028 §5) |
| Observability | Azure Application Insights + structlog |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions |
| API docs | FastAPI Swagger + ReDoc |
| MCP | FastMCP (PrefectHQ) — 8 curated tools at `/mcp` |
| Python tooling | conda + Black + Ruff + mypy + pytest + Bandit |
| Frontend tooling | Prettier + ESLint + Vitest + React Testing Library |
| Secret scanning | betterleaks (pre-commit + CI) |
| SAST | Bandit + CodeQL |

### Client-side MCP servers (`.mcp.json`)

Distinct from DataQ's **own** FastMCP server at `/mcp` (ADR 0008 — the 8 tools DataQ *serves* to AI clients), the repo-root **`.mcp.json`** configures MCP servers that AI assistants working in this repo *consume*:

| Server | Package (pinned major) | Publisher | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context7` | `@upstash/context7-mcp@1` (npx) | Upstash | Up-to-date library docs lookup while coding |
| `azure` | `@azure/mcp@3.0.0-beta.29` (npx) — **exact**, see caveats | Microsoft (`github.com/microsoft/mcp`) | Container Apps / Key Vault / Monitor + App Insights KQL without hand-rolled `az rest` — the 2026-07-13 outage was invisible in `/healthz` and only the telemetry showed the exporter log loop |

- **Trust prompt:** Claude Code prompts once per machine before starting servers from a project `.mcp.json`; approve only if the list above matches what's in the file.
- **Pin majors, not `latest`** — same rationale as the GX pin.
- **Supply-chain cadence:** quarterly audit per CONTRIBUTING.md rule 39 (deprecated/yanked/publisher-transfer check before any bump).
- **`azure` caveats (deliberate, re-check before relying on it):** `@azure/mcp`'s only dist-tag is a **beta** (`3.0.0-beta.29`) — Microsoft-published, but pre-stable, so treat tool-surface changes as expected. **This is the one entry pinned to an exact version, not a major**, and deliberately so: npm excludes prereleases from a bare major range, so `@azure/mcp@3` resolves to *nothing* (`E404 No match found for version 3`) and the server would fail to launch. The "pin majors" rule assumes a package with a stable major; this one has none, so the version moves only on a conscious bump. It authenticates through the **local `az` CLI credential**, so it inherits whatever that identity can do — use it for reading state, and keep the Key Vault rule intact: **never surface or print a secret value**. Microsoft telemetry is disabled via `AZURE_MCP_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=false` in the server env. It is only useful while the Azure estate is up — drop the entry if the wind-down completes.

**Not added, and why** (so the decision isn't re-litigated): a **Postgres MCP** was evaluated for run/result triage and rejected on supply-chain grounds. The reference `@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres` is **deprecated**; the npm `postgres-mcp` is published by a single unaffiliated maintainer; the PyPI `postgres-mcp` declares **no license**, which CONTRIBUTING rule 40 / ADR 0031 forbids outright. `psql` over Bash already covers the need with zero added surface.

622	
623	| Status | Task | Theme / gap |
624	|---|---|---|
625	<<<<<<< Updated upstream
626	| ✅ | [#1325](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1325) **Scale-aware execution** (`Fixes #595`) — a `sampling` block on the run target (`head` / `random`, optional seed) that the flat-file + UC runners honour with a genuinely bounded read, plus a size-probe guardrail (`RUN_MAX_SCAN_BYTES` 128 MiB / `RUN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS` 1.5M) that refuses *before* materialising rather than OOM-killing the child (#755's other half). Sampled-ness lands on `results.sampling` (new nullable JSONB) per **check**, not per run — a volume monitor pushes down and is exact while the expectations beside it saw 100k of 5M, and one flag would have to lie about one of them; `sampled` is explicit, so a "sample" covering the whole dataset is reported as the complete read it is. Sampling is **refused at save time** on Snowflake/Iceberg and never applied to freshness (a MAX over a sample is a smaller maximum → healthy data reported critically stale). Measured, §W6 of [perf-baseline.md](perf-baseline.md): a 249 MB / 5M-row CSV needs **2,210 MiB** uncapped, is refused in **0.00 s** capped, and runs at **411 MiB / 0.15 s** sampled. The first cap draft (256 MiB) was wrong and the measurement is what caught it — that CSV passes it and still OOMs. **Live UC verification done 2026-08-14** (the #953 rule): head + random draws live, `TABLESAMPLE (p PERCENT)` fixed-point literals down to the `0.000001` floor parse, `REPEATABLE(7)` reproduced identical 50-row draws twice, and a live `run_checks` stamped `sampling` on every result | Theme 7 / G-b |
627	| ✅ | [#327](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/327) Batch the profiler's N+1 per-column queries — [#1323](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1323). Rank driver LEFT-joined to one derived table per column, chunked at 25 (measured: a single 50-way join costs 3x a 25-way one, Postgres switches to its genetic optimiser at 12 relations). The obvious `UNION ALL` shape was built first and rejected by Postgres — a union unifies branch types, and even NULL-padded per-column slots resolve pairwise left-to-right, so padding settles on `text` before the owning branch is reached. It compiled cleanly; only a live run found it. **Live Snowflake + Unity Catalog verification DONE 2026-08-14 pre-merge** (#953): equivalence + type fidelity PASS on both warehouses, batched 4.5×/5.2× faster, synthetic 25-way join shows no planner cliff on either | Theme 7 |

### v1.1 W6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close (due 2026-08-15) — 1/14

| ✅ | [#1325](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1325) **Scale-aware execution** (`Fixes #595`) — a `sampling` block on the run target (`head` / `random`, optional seed) that the flat-file + UC runners honour with a genuinely bounded read, plus a size-probe guardrail (`RUN_MAX_SCAN_BYTES` 128 MiB / `RUN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS` 1.5M) that refuses *before* materialising rather than OOM-killing the child (#755's other half). Sampled-ness lands on `results.sampling` (new nullable JSONB) per **check**, not per run — a volume monitor pushes down and is exact while the expectations beside it saw 100k of 5M, and one flag would have to lie about one of them; `sampled` is explicit, so a "sample" covering the whole dataset is reported as the complete read it is. Sampling is **refused at save time** on Snowflake/Iceberg and never applied to freshness (a MAX over a sample is a smaller maximum → healthy data reported critically stale). Measured, §W6 of [perf-baseline.md](perf-baseline.md): a 249 MB / 5M-row CSV needs **2,210 MiB** uncapped, is refused in **0.00 s** capped, and runs at **411 MiB / 0.15 s** sampled. The first cap draft (256 MiB) was wrong and the measurement is what caught it — that CSV passes it and still OOMs. **Live UC verification done 2026-08-14** (the #953 rule): head + random draws live, `TABLESAMPLE (p PERCENT)` fixed-point literals down to the `0.000001` floor parse, `REPEATABLE(7)` reproduced identical 50-row draws twice, and a live `run_checks` stamped `sampling` on every result | Theme 7 / G-b |

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Verdicts on the four questions

**Q1 — does `validateFields()` return unmounted fields?** Confirmed **no**, the PR's comment is right. `@rc-component/form@1.8.5` (antd 6.5.1's form engine, at `frontend/node_modules/.pnpm/@rc-component+form@1.8.5_*/node_modules/@rc-component/form/es/hooks/useForm.js`): `validateFields` (L741) builds its value name-path list from `this.getFieldEntities(true)` — registered entities only — and resolves with `getFieldsValue(namePathList)`; `getFieldsValue()` (L208) short-circuits to the raw store *only* for `getFieldsValue(true)`. Unmount with the default `preserve` keeps the value in the store but removes the entity, so the value vanishes from `validateFields()`. I traced every edit-mode path and **none of them silently drops or corrupts a stored block today** — the "connections list missing the suite's connection" case makes `kind` null, which the existing `hadTarget && target === null` guard catches with a visible error (`SuiteForm.tsx:137-141`), and `listConnections` is unfiltered/unpaginated (`backend/app/api/v1/connections.py:248`), so it can't happen anyway. The one residual hole is finding #4 below.

**Q2 — no defect.** `backend/app/services/suite_service.py:204-216` **replaces** `suite.target` wholesale (`suite.target = target`); a target without `sampling` clears the stored block. Toggling to "Whole dataset" does the right thing.

**Q3 — no defect.** `initEntityValue` (useForm.js:503-514) writes `initialValue` only `if (prevValue === undefined)`, and `registerField` (L525) uses `resetWithFieldInitialValue({entities:[entity], skipExist: true})`, which at L407 only writes when `!info.skipExist || originValue === undefined`. A later-mounting `sampling_strategy` with `initialValue="head"` cannot clobber a `'random'` set earlier by `setFieldsValue`. Mount ordering is also safe (child `componentDidMount` → `sampling_enabled` initialValue `false` runs *before* SuiteForm's `useEffect`, which then overrides).

**Q4 — no defect.** `useWatch` reads the whole store (`getFieldsValue(true)`) independently of field registration, and `SamplingFields` unmounting when `canSample` is false takes its watches with it. No stale state.

618	renders bands + baseline overlay; threshold ordering validated at authoring (#568); the
619	results/connections UX batch (#345/#283/#351/#424/#349) merged.
620	
621	### v1.1 W6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close (due 2026-08-15) — 3/14
622	
623	| Status | Task | Theme / gap |
624	|---|---|---|
625	| ✅ | [#1325](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1325) **Scale-aware execution** (`Fixes #595`) — a `sampling` block on the run target (`head` / `random`, optional seed) that the flat-file + UC runners honour with a genuinely bounded read, plus a size-probe guardrail (`RUN_MAX_SCAN_BYTES` 128 MiB / `RUN_MAX_SCAN_ROWS` 1.5M) that refuses *before* materialising rather than OOM-killing the child (#755's other half). Sampled-ness lands on `results.sampling` (new nullable JSONB) per **check**, not per run — a volume monitor pushes down and is exact while the expectations beside it saw 100k of 5M, and one flag would have to lie about one of them; `sampled` is explicit, so a "sample" covering the whole dataset is reported as the complete read it is. Sampling is **refused at save time** on Snowflake/Iceberg and never applied to freshness (a MAX over a sample is a smaller maximum → healthy data reported critically stale). Measured, §W6 of [perf-baseline.md](perf-baseline.md): a 249 MB / 5M-row CSV needs **2,210 MiB** uncapped, is refused in **0.00 s** capped, and runs at **411 MiB / 0.15 s** sampled. The first cap draft (256 MiB) was wrong and the measurement is what caught it — that CSV passes it and still OOMs. **Live UC verification done 2026-08-14** (the #953 rule): head + random draws live, `TABLESAMPLE (p PERCENT)` fixed-point literals down to the `0.000001` floor parse, `REPEATABLE(7)` reproduced identical 50-row draws twice, and a live `run_checks` stamped `sampling` on every result. **The deferred UI half landed in [#1333](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1333)** — a per-check `Sampled` tag + a run-level caveat on run detail, and the authoring block in the suite form, offered only on the three capable datasources (the backend 422s a spec elsewhere, so a control there would have exactly one outcome: a save error). Two rules carried across from the backend: the caveat is claimed only when `sampling.sampled` is true, never a derived `rows < total_rows` (a "sample" of 100 rows from a 40-row file covered everything, and badging it would train the reader to skip the caveat that matters — #424's lesson on a second field); and the form **refuses** a sampling block it cannot honour rather than dropping it, since a silent drop leaves an author believing a nightly 100M-row suite is bounded when it is not | Theme 7 / G-b |
626	| ✅ | [#327](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/327) Batch the profiler's N+1 per-column queries — [#1323](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1323).
